title: Rava of Barnish
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman says he always discusses matters with Rav Ashi, as in Shabbat 28a, where he said to Rav Ashi, “One can refute…” — “rather, Rava of Barnish said”; in Rosh Hashanah 26b he said to Rav Ashi, “If I had been there I would have said to him: How did he ‘kava’ you [i.e., rob you]?” etc.; in Bava Metzia 73b he said to Rav Ashi, “Let the Master see the Rabbis who eat interest”; and in Zevachim 11a he said to Rav Ashi, “But let us refute… — rather,” etc.
Hyman infers from this that he took part with Rav Ashi in arranging the Talmud.
In Nazir 31a and 40a we find that he spoke to Rava; Hyman suggests that possibly it was written לרב״א, an abbreviation for Rav Ashi.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Rosh Hashanah 26b establishes קבע as rob in this episode. The unfamiliar word remains visible in the translated question, rather than being mistranslated fix. The always assertion, Talmud-arrangement inference and proposed Rav-Ashi abbreviation remain Hyman’s.
Hyman’s “always” and his inference concerning participation in arranging the Talmud are retained. The Rava/Rav Ashi abbreviation proposal remains his conjecture.
